name: Core
description: Core node catalog — infrastructure + storage + windows + scripts + api routes

apps.title: Graph
apps.description: A node graph canvas. Every graph in a space is one instance of this app; each is addressed as <space>.<graph>, and the space's own page shows its default graph. Removing the instance removes the graph and everything on it.

actions.label: Set SSH Key
actions.description: Assign a Key Store key to this server (key reference is "<keyStoreNodeId>:<keyName>"). With install=true, also append the key's public half to the remote's authorized_keys using the server's current credentials.

install.description: Also install the public key on the remote's authorized_keys (default: false)

actions.label: Accept Host Key
actions.description: Scan the remote host key and pin it into known_hosts so OpenSSH-based transports (e.g. docker over ssh://) stop failing host-key verification.

actions.label: Generate Key
actions.description: Generate a new SSH keypair in this Key Store. Returns the key name and type — never private key material.

actions.label: List Keys
actions.description: List keys in this store with their type and fingerprint. Does not expose private key material.

actions.label: Delete Key
actions.description: Delete a key (and its public key) from this store.

name.description: Name of the key to delete

actions.label: Generate Secret
actions.description: Create or rotate a secret with a server-side random value. Absent name creates it, existing name rotates it. Returns the name and created/rotated status — never the value.

name.description: Secret name to create or rotate

actions.label: List Secrets
actions.description: List the secret names in this store. Names only — no action on this node type returns a value.

actions.label: Delete Secret
actions.description: Delete a secret from this store by name. Refused, naming the nodes, while any node still references it — through a `secrets` field, an `apiKeySecret` field, or a `secret:NAME` value anywhere in its data. Those nodes resolve the name at their next deploy, run or session start, and a container already running keeps the value it resolved at startup, so the break would not surface until then. A node type that names a secret some other way is not seen, so no refusal means nothing matched those three conventions rather than nothing references the name. Pass allowUnclean to delete it anyway and leave the reference dangling.

name.description: Name of the secret to delete

allowUnclean.description: Delete even while nodes still reference the name (default: false)

actions.label: Run
actions.description: Execute the script in the connected terminal context (or local if none).

actions.description: Execute the script in the connected terminal context (or local if none).

actions.label: Send
actions.description: Deliver a message into a group-chat thread — same delivery as a wired text-in payload, with the sender attributed from what fed the run. Delivered only when the sender is a member of the thread's chat; refused, clearly, for an unknown or unauthorized thread. Returns the thread reference and whether the message queued behind a running turn or was delivered immediately. Never the message content.

thread.description: A group-chat thread reference ("<group-slug>.<agent-slug>.<thread-slug>", a whole session key, or a thread id) to deliver into

queue.description: How this message relates to anything already waiting for that agent. "wait" holds it until the turn in progress ends, then delivers it on its own. "push" interrupts that turn and delivers everything held at once, this message last, so the agent reads the whole picture before acting — use it when what you are sending changes what the agent should be doing. With nothing already waiting the two are the same ordinary send. Required: sending into a session that may be busy is a choice, not a default. Replaces the former "force", which was this same interrupt-and-deliver-everything.

contexts.label: Terminal Context
contexts.description: Terminal execution context (local, WSL, or SSH)
